gloss: to leave over; to leave (something) remaining; to have to spare

definitions.gloss: to leave (something) over; to leave remaining
definitions.explanation: To leave a portion of something unused, unfinished, or unconsumed. The transitive counterpart of {余|あま}る.
Used in fixed expressions like {〜|〜}を{余|あま}して to mean 'with (time/distance) to spare' before reaching a deadline or destination.

examples.japanese: ご{飯|はん}を{余|あま}した。
examples.english: I left some rice over (didn't finish it).

examples.japanese: {力|ちから}を{余|あま}して{勝|か}った。
examples.english: He won with energy to spare.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}を{十分|じゅうぶん}{余|あま}して{駅|えき}に{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: I arrived at the station with plenty of time to spare.

examples.japanese: おかずを{少|すこ}し{余|あま}して{弟|おとうと}に{残|のこ}しておいた。
examples.english: I left a bit of the side dish over and saved it for my younger brother.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{締|し}め{切|き}りまで{一|いち}{時間|じかん}{余|あま}して{原稿|げんこう}を{書|か}き{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: He finished writing the manuscript with an hour to spare before the deadline.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べきれずに{料理|りょうり}を{半分|はんぶん}も{余|あま}してしまった。
examples.english: I couldn't finish it and ended up leaving half the food over.
examples.notes: {〜|〜}してしまう adds the nuance of regret or unintended outcome.

notes:
{余|あま}す is the transitive counterpart of {余|あま}る (to be left over). The pair forms a classic transitive/intransitive set: someone {余|あま}す something, vs. something {余|あま}る on its own.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Transitive: ご{飯|はん}を{余|あま}す (to leave rice over) — the speaker actively leaves it
- Intransitive: ご{飯|はん}が{余|あま}る (the rice is left over) — it simply remains

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間|じかん}を{余|あま}す: to have time to spare
- {力|ちから}を{余|あま}す: to have energy/strength to spare
- {〜|〜}を{〜|〜}{時間|じかん}{余|あま}して: with (number of) hours to spare
- {持|も}て{余|あま}す: to be unable to handle (a separate fixed compound — see related)

USAGE:
- Sense 1 (leaving food/material over) is much less common in everyday speech than {残|のこ}す, which is the default verb for leaving food on a plate. {余|あま}す sounds slightly stiff or literary in this sense.
- Sense 2 ({時間|じかん}を{余|あま}して, etc.) is the more frequently encountered pattern, especially in sports commentary and news.

RELATED WORDS:
- {余|あま}る: intransitive counterpart — to be left over
- {残|のこ}す: to leave behind (more common for food/items)
- {持|も}て{余|あま}す: to be at a loss with; to find too much to handle

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {余|あま}していませんでした
